newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH seeks control of U.S. luxury goods distributor.
newsitem.headline: LVMH seeks control of U.S. luxury goods distributor.

text.p: French luxury goods group LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton said on Wednesday that it had struck an agreement to acquire 58.75 percent of San Francisco-based luxury goods distributor DFS.
"The price of this acquisition will be 12.6 billion francs ($2.5 billion) ," LVMH said in a statement.
DFS is the world's largest luxury products distributor with annual sales of more than 15 billion francs, 180 boutiques and 20 years' experience in retailing in Asia, LVMH said.
"Thanks to this acquisition, LVMH will increase its presence in the Asia-Pacific region and emerging countries, a future growth area," it said.
The company said it would keep DFS's management team in place, and said the group would be managed independently of LVMH's other businesses.
It said in its statement that the acquisition agreement hinges on certain conditions but did not elaborate. Company officials were not immediately available for comment.

The New York Times reported on Wednesday that billionaire Robert Miller, who owns 38.75 percent of the DFS duty-free store empire, was trying to block a sale by his partners. It reported Miller said the deal would violate the terms of an agreement he signed in 1991 with his partners.
